text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on June 6. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The security police arrested the bankruptcy receiver of Oru peat plant who will probably be accused of carelessness, police said. Kuusk earlier this week said he was threatened with a car bomb and had to throw the wages destined for the bankrupt plant onto the road.
- The interior ministry appointed two assistants to the director of the police department director and a new prefect to Harju county arond Tallinn as the first steps of a reform of police reform.
- President Lennart Meri promoted the commander of the Estonian defence forces, Johannes Kert, to major general aboard a visiting NATO plane Boeing AWACS E-3D.
- The education ministry plans to send textbooks to an Estonian school in Abkhazia, an official said.
- Speakers of European parliaments will meet in Tallinn on June 7, a parliament spokesman said.
- The Traditional Days of the Old Town begin in Tallinn on June 7 with concerts, walking tours and sports events.

- The chairman of Hoiupank Olari Taal intends to found the first private nature protection area in Estonia on the 61 hectares of land he bought at Noarootsi near the presidential summer residence in western Estonia.
- Saku announced its which showed a 5.3 million kroon profit in the four months of 1997.
